part_title: PrivateLink, Endpoint Service Security and GenAI Network Review

scenes.title: What is AWS PrivateLink?
scenes.narration: Follow the consumer application in one VPC to its interface endpoint with a private IP address. On the provider side, an endpoint service exposes a particular application behind a Network Load Balancer. AWS PrivateLink connects the consumer endpoint to that specific service without requiring an internet gateway or full CIDR-to-CIDR routing between the VPCs. The comparison table contrasts PrivateLink with peering. Peering provides broader routed network communication, whereas PrivateLink lets a provider publish a specific service to approved consumers. This is useful for a shared enterprise AI tool, internal API or supported SaaS integration. Private networking doesn't automatically identify the end user or authorise business operations, so the provider must still implement appropriate application authentication. Verify connection permissions, DNS and service availability before using it. The lesson is granular private service connectivity rather than joining all of the networks together.

scenes.title: VPC endpoint services and permissions
scenes.narration: This diagram focuses on the control-plane steps for PrivateLink. First, the provider places its application behind a Network Load Balancer and creates a VPC endpoint service. It configures allowed principals that may request connections. Next, an authorised consumer creates an interface endpoint in its own subnets referring to that endpoint service. Depending on the service settings, the provider may also need to accept the endpoint connection. Finally, the consumer's private application sends traffic through the endpoint to the provider targets. Separate three questions: who is permitted to create the endpoint, whether the provider accepts the connection, and whether the application authorises the actual API call. The slide mentions endpoint policies; do not assume policies on a custom endpoint service automatically authorise arbitrary application methods. Endpoint policy support differs from permissions enforced by the custom backend. Check IAM, security groups, acceptance state, service DNS and backend authentication rather than relying only on a green endpoint status.

scenes.title: VPC Security Closing Checklist
scenes.narration: The closing checklist is a practical network-security review. Inspect whether public subnets contain only deliberate entry points while application servers and databases stay in private subnets. Confirm that route tables send traffic to the intended internet gateway, NAT gateway or private service endpoint. Review security groups for least-privilege traffic between application layers and inspect ACL rules where subnet filtering is necessary. Then examine VPC Flow Logs for useful network evidence and confirm encryption for sensitive stores. The diagram connects a public load balancer, private application tiers, endpoint paths and route tables. Do not confuse a private subnet with an absence of all egress; a NAT route can still provide outbound internet connectivity. Likewise, an endpoint can exist while an IAM policy denies the request. Record the effective paths and run tests before approving a GenAI system for production. This checklist verifies the boundaries; it is not a substitute for model safety or data-governance controls.

scenes.title: Secure GenAI application reference architecture
scenes.narration: This architecture brings the security services together. A user's request reaches Route 53 DNS, passes AWS WAF inspection, and enters an Application Load Balancer in public subnets. Application compute runs in private subnets and uses permitted VPC endpoints to call Amazon Bedrock. Secrets Manager protects credentials for downstream tools, KMS-backed encryption protects stored information, and CloudWatch monitors operational behavior. Observe the trust boundaries: untrusted internet traffic at the edge, private application networking, access to managed models, and protected data or secrets. Each boundary has a different control. WAF doesn't replace IAM, a security group doesn't validate a user's JWT, and encryption doesn't prevent an authorised-but-overprivileged service from misusing data. For resilient operation, deploy across appropriate Availability Zones and configure service-specific endpoint access. The key architectural lesson is defence in depth: verify who can call each component and what information may cross each boundary.

scenes.title: Identity decision guide
scenes.narration: Start with the identity question across the top: is this an AWS workload, a workforce member or an end user of your application? A Lambda function, container or EC2 workload normally needs an IAM role with temporary credentials to call AWS APIs. Employees accessing multiple AWS accounts are better served by IAM Identity Center and centrally assigned permission sets. An IAM user is a separate identity with credentials and may be appropriate in limited circumstances, but shouldn't be the default for federated workforce access. Customer-facing login belongs in an identity system such as a Cognito user pool, which returns authentication tokens. If the application client needs temporary AWS credentials for direct access to resources like S3, a Cognito identity pool can broker an IAM role session. Those two Cognito components solve different problems and may be used together. Match the identity type to the caller and the access required, then enforce least privilege on the resulting session. A successful sign-in never automatically means unrestricted application access.
